rules: Fill only what the product's photos or its text show. Never guess and never invent: leave a part empty when it is not visible or not stated.
Pick tags from the catalogue, on their path. Tags waiting for approval may be used too. A tag the catalogue lacks goes in new_tags only, with its full path, the shop's words and why.
Tags are lower-case kebab-case (braided-round-cord). Fonts are written as the family is named in fonts.json.
Do not give fit words, the audience or the category: LAB fills them from its own measurements and the shop.

Do not write centimetres. Draw a box instead: an art, each text inside it and each label or patch gets a box on the job's measure_photo (the photo LAB measures: the whole garment, no model), as [x1, y1, x2, y2], each 0-1 of the photo's width and height. LAB measures it in cm (its size, how far from the HPS, CB or waistband and from the centre). Box on another photo only what that photo does not show; it then comes without cm.
An art is one printed, embroidered or applied graphic area of the garment, or a label, patch or tab sewn on it.

Every separate text inside an art is its own element: its exact words, its closest font, its own effect and its own box. Two lines in two different fonts or treatments are two elements (e.g. 'UNDER GROUND' faded in a stencil font, 'GLOBAL CLUB / BUILT BELOW THE SURFACE' plain in a sans serif).
An art's technique is split: technique (e.g. plastisol, puff-print, embroidery), finish (matt, glossy…), effect (faded, cracked, rusted…). dtm: true when the art is in the fabric's own colour.

A label, a patch or a tab is an art (kind: label / patch), described in full: its purpose, make (woven-damask, satin, taffeta, printed, rubber…), fold, finish (matt, glossy…), the exact words on it with their font, and its box. Its colours are read by LAB from its boxes.
Colours are never written: for each art, box it on each colour's own photo (by_colour) and LAB reads its Pantone there, and the fabric's Pantone from each colour's photo.
gsm is a number of grams per square metre: the shop's when stated, else your estimate from how the fabric looks and falls (it is marked as estimated).
A part's details are kebab-case tags (self-colour, frayed-edge, matt, gun-black), never a sentence.
Treatments (washes, distressing…) describe the style: they apply to every colour.
A trim's parts follow the catalogue (a drawcord: Cord, Ends, Exit, Stopper; a zip: Chain, Opening, Tape, Slider, Puller, Placement). Two of one item (rib cuffs and a rib hem) are two entries.
photos_to_delete: suggest photos that add nothing (duplicates, no product, another style). They are only suggestions: nothing is deleted.
Answer with one JSON block exactly in the answer format, every job of this round in it, nothing else in the block.

fabrics.fabric: <a tag from Fabric > Woven / Knitted / Non-woven / Seamless>

label.purpose: <for a label or patch: main-label, flag-label, hem-tab…>

arts.photo: <the job's measure_photo (box it there when it shows there; another photo only when the art is not on it)>
arts.box: [x1, y1, x2, y2] on that photo, each 0-1 of its width / height (top-left 0,0)

elements.box: [x1, y1, x2, y2] on that photo, each 0-1 of its width / height (top-left 0,0)

<each colour of the product, as named in.box: [x1, y1, x2, y2] on that photo, each 0-1 of its width / height (top-left 0,0)

details: <kebab-case tags of what is visible: material, colour, finish, design, e.g. self-colour, frayed-edge>

new_tags.path: Trims and details > Drawcord > Ends > Aglet

jobs.evidence: <which words or photos each choice rests on>
jobs.could_not_tell: <what the photos and text do not show>

מכנסיים בגזרה ישרה ונינוחה שיושבים מעולה על הגוף. עשויים מבד קורדרוי איכותי, רך ומחמם שמתאים בול לעונה הקרה. כוללים גומי במותן עם שרוך קשירה, כיסי צד נוחים ופסי קנט קונטרסטיים לאורך הצדדים והכיסים האחוריים. פריט אורבני ייחודי שמשלב נוחות מרבית עם מראה מוקפד ליום-יום.
